chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Hammad ibn Waqid al-Lahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man were to spend whatever was in his hands in the way of Allah, it would not be better, nor would he be successful.
Is it not that Allah the Exalted says: 'And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, and do good; surely Allah loves the doers of good'?
ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about spending too much in charity or God's cause?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the notion that extreme generosity is always virtuous, emphasizing that self-inflicted financial ruin contradicts divine wisdom. He interprets the 'doers of good' (*al-muhsinin*) in the Quranic context as those who practice *iqtisad* (moderation), aligning with the Shia scholarly principle that balance in worldly affairs is a form of worship. This highlights the practical implication that preserving one's ability to continue serving Allah and society requires avoiding excess that leads to depletion.
